Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed August 17, 2026, 9:21 AM ET / 13:21 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The PR preserves reply-mode context through embedded and CLI-backed message tools and makes Reef targetless direct replies reuse the inbound message thread. ## Regression provenance Possible regression — probable (reproduction; reviewed change). No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 4 items remain** Keep open: current main drops the prepared reply policy before generic message tools, and this branch carries it through the embedded and CLI paths. No concrete patch defect was found, but merge readiness requires after-fix boundary proof and direct Codex-contract inspection for the PR’s Codex MCP claim. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `c9021a0d34ffddc0ec2aa8f66ef13d991beef80d` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | PR readiness rating was derived from proof quality, review findings, security review, and reviewer confidence. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 6 items | Current-main defect path: Current main constructs generic threading context without replyToMode; the message-action sender defaults an absent mode to off, so a same-conversation targetless send cannot inherit the inbound message identifier.
Owner-boundary repair: The branch supplies the prepared mode to embedded context, CLI grants, loopback request context, scoped tool resolution, and the cache key; Reef then supplies the matching inbound thread anchor only for its own transport.
Existing delivery invariant: The message-action boundary only injects replyTo for the same conversation and an all/first policy, while Reef’s outbound adapter transmits both thread and reply identifiers. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Inbound channel turns prepare a reply policy and message identity for agent tools. Message sending then uses that context to attach a transport reply identifier, which lets a waiting conversation turn recognize the response. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Inbound Reef message] --> B[Prepared reply context] B --> C[Embedded or CLI agent] C --> D[Targetless message tool] D --> E[Reef outbound reply] E --> F[Conversation correlation] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should this PR obtain exact-head Reef correlation proof before merge rather than defer the first after-fix two-agent verification until after merge? | **Require before-merge correlation proof:** Run the two-agent Reef flow on the PR head and record that the transport reply has replyToId and conversations_turn returns replied. | Why: The repository requires boundary or live proof for delivery/session behavior, and the available evidence only demonstrates the pre-fix failure plus unit-level propagation. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - After-fix evidence is limited to unit tests and build/check claims; it does not yet show a targetless Reef tool send carrying replyToId and yielding a correlated conversations_turn result. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The PR invokes a Codex MCP compatibility claim, but direct inspection of the required sibling Codex source was unavailable. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The bug fix has a net +46 production-line increase across context boundaries; that propagation appears necessary for explicit ownership, but it should be validated at the delivery boundary before merge.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Capture end-to-end Reef proof before merge (recommended)** Use the exact PR head to show a targetless same-target send receives the inbound reply and thread identifiers and the initiating conversation completes. 2. **Pause for proof** Hold the branch until an authorized two-agent run or approved mock-gateway harness verifies the delivery and correlation boundary. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep reply policy explicit across the existing embedded, CLI, and loopback boundaries, then prove the exact PR head with two authorized Reef agents or the approved mock-gateway harness before merging. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: current main omits replyToMode from tool context while the message-action boundary treats a missing mode as off. The supplied live pre-fix report is consistent with that path, but this review did not execute authorized Reef agents. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes, provisionally: carrying the admission-time policy through the existing context boundaries is more maintainable than inferring correlation downstream. Its real delivery and correlation effect still needs boundary proof. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. - Direct dependency contract inspection used current sibling Codex `origin/main` at `8e89e98cf6d4d79f7add5c04ddd4bbd76b1594a1`; its MCP connection manager and RMCP client pass the JSON tool arguments through unchanged, so the new reply policy remains OpenClaw-owned loopback context.

ClawSweeper rank-up move / skip: I am not deploying this unmerged PR head to the two production-like agents. The operator explicitly chose the consistency contract “merge the PR, update all installs to the latest main, then test; worst case, use a follow-up PR.” The pre-fix live run already proved the transport failure boundary. Immediately after merge, both installations will be pinned to one immutable merged `main` SHA and the two authorized Reef directions will be live-tested; any remaining defect will be repaired in a follow-up PR.

The reported “persistent cache schema” is not a stored-data change: `McpLoopbackToolCache` is process-local and short-lived. Adding `replyToMode` to its cache key prevents closures prepared under different reply policies from sharing one row; it adds no persisted state, migration, or schema version.

Merged via squash.

- Prepared head SHA: [e6e23b546688dab2c0da6927bbedce972360b743](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/125283/commits/e6e23b546688dab2c0da6927bbedce972360b743)
- Landed commit: [793669c8f6ddfad07b40009068f532832685b7d6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/793669c8f6ddfad07b40009068f532832685b7d6)

Post-merge live proof completed on exact main SHA `793669c8f6ddfad07b40009068f532832685b7d6`.

Both authorized installations were pinned to that SHA before messaging. Clawstudio → Roboclaw and Roboclaw → Clawstudio each completed inline with a persisted conversation-delivery status of `replied`; each reply carried `replyToId` equal to the exact reserved outbound message ID and contained the requested exact text.

The original failing path was exercised directly: Roboclaw answered the inbound Reef turn through a targetless `message.send`, and the returned Reef message correlated successfully instead of timing out. The reverse direction independently ran the receiving Clawstudio agent and completed the initiating `conversations_turn` with `status: replied`.

All four outbound Reef messages have one `proposal`, one allowed `guard_verdict`, one `envelope`, and one signed `confirm_delivery` with status `accepted`. Final health and readiness are HTTP 200 on both installations; both Reef accounts are configured, running, connected, lifecycle `ready`, with no last error and no degraded event loop.
